summary: Railroad fire lookout on Red Mountain: a stone cabin built in 1909 and staffed to watch the snow sheds until 1934; a 2023 blog post says it was visible from the highway at the Cisco exit.

facts.design: Stone cabin built in 1909 to replace an 1876 wooden station

staffing.status: two fire watchers round the clock until 1934

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Tahoe National Forest
facts.status_note: Abandoned by the railroad in 1934; not an active lookout.

events.note: Central Pacific Railroad fire lookout station below Signal Peak; original structure was wooden
Southern Pacific replaced the wooden structure with a stone cabin
Lookout witnessed a motorcycle rider go over the grade into the Yuba River and passed word to Cisco; a rescue party followed
Newspaper report that lightning struck the isolated cabin and apparently killed the man stationed there

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1909 date is the current stone cabin. The register and CPRR history show a wooden Central Pacific station from 1876 that the stone cabin replaced.

notes_for_editor: History is well sourced across the register, the CPRR museum page and the forest lookouts page. Current condition rests on one 2023 blog sketch seen from the highway; no source gives current access, ownership details or a physical inspection, so no access or visit facts are recorded. The AllTrails trail page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The record's county (Nevada) matches the forest lookouts page header. The 1920 and 1931 items are newspaper reports quoted on the forest lookouts page; the 1931 item names the man who died, which the story leaves out.
